title: Chlorine gas incident
stem: A chlorine leak at a public swimming pool plant room. Fire services report 12 casualties coming to your ED; the first arrives in 5 minutes, still in wet clothes. The first patient, a 35-year-old pool worker, is coughing and wheezy. Prepare the department, then manage him.
notes:
Checked against the UK CBRN/HAZMAT guidance (NHS England 'Initial Operational Response' — Remove, Remove, Remove, 2023), UKHSA chlorine toxicological overview (2022), and the Hong Kong HA/Fire Services decontamination practice.

Prepare: activate the hospital major incident/HAZMAT plan; lock down the ED entrance so contaminated patients do not walk in; set up decontamination outside (hot/warm/cold zones, upwind); staff in appropriate PPE (powered respirator/level C for decontamination); ask about the agent (chlorine: intermediate water solubility, forms hydrochloric and hypochlorous acid on mucosa). Decontamination: remove the casualty from the source, disrobe (removes most contamination), bag clothes, then wash skin and irrigate eyes with water; chlorine gas itself leaves little residue, but wet clothing holds it. Treatment is supportive: high-flow humidified oxygen, nebulised salbutamol for bronchospasm, eye irrigation, CXR and gas; nebulised sodium bicarbonate (4.2%) is used by some with weak evidence; routine steroids are not recommended; intubate for severe hypoxia/ARDS with lung-protective ventilation. Most symptoms appear early, but pulmonary oedema can develop over hours — observe symptomatic patients (at least 6 hours; admit if hypoxic or CXR changes).

Your notes list 'Chlorine gas incident' as a topic only. The nebulised bicarbonate point is weakly supported — present it as an option, not a standard.

opts.r: Contaminated clothing can put the ED and staff out of action.

steps.label: Fire officer
steps.hint: What agent, how many, how long exposed, any decontamination done?

Incident.r: Chlorine gas from mixing pool chemicals. Leak now contained.
12: 3 short of breath, the rest coughing and sore eyes.
They were moved into fresh air; no disrobing yet.

steps.label: Decontaminate
steps.hint: Remove from source, disrobe and bag, wash skin, irrigate eyes, then into the ED.

opts.t: Disrobe outside; clothes in a sealed labelled bag
Irrigate the eyes with water or saline
Wash the skin with lukewarm water
Into resus via the clean route

steps.label: Treat
steps.hint: Humidified high-flow oxygen, nebulised salbutamol; bicarbonate nebs optional; no routine steroids.

steps.label: Investigations
steps.hint: Gas and chest X-ray; later film if he worsens.

Now.r: pH 7.36, PaO2 8.2 kPa on oxygen, PaCO2 4.6.
At 4 hours, worse hypoxia; bilateral hazy airspace shadowing.

steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Admit hypoxic patients; observe the others at least 6 hours; ICU if worsening; public health.

opts.t: ICU: hypoxic chemical pneumonitis — may need lung-protective ventilation

opts.t: Observe the other symptomatic patients at least 6 hours
Inform the Poison Information Centre and Department of Health
opts.mark: Informs poisons centre and public health

opts.t: Discharge the coughing patients now if SpO2 is normal
opts.r: Pulmonary oedema can develop over hours.

badge.name: Clean Zone
badge.flavor: Lock down, strip, wash, then treat. No antidote — oxygen and salbutamol.

cards.q: First step for a HAZMAT casualty?
options: Take them straight to resus for oxygen
Give antibiotics and nebulisers in triage
Remove from area, remove clothing, remove contamination
Remove all staff from the department
Remove other patients from the ED
The clean area beside the ED entrance

options: No observation if SpO2 is normal
